annotations.annotation_text: Page 195 opens Book 1, Chapter 7 ("Shem the Penman") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions, featuring Shem, Shaun (as Justius), ALP (Mercius). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "Anna Livia" on page 195 ("Shem the Penman"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. In this Age of Gods passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart
